On this page

Project Policy ​

Per-project agent permissions, declared in each project's memory file (memory/projects/<name>.md) as a small YAML-ish frontmatter block.

markdown
---
branch: new        # new | current
approval: confirm  # confirm | auto
verify: npm test   # optional shell command run after a work delegation commits
---

Keys ​

branch ​

ValueBehaviour
new (default)Cuts a saidi/* branch and opens a PR
currentCommits on the checked-out branch

approval ​

ValueBehaviour
confirm (default)Asks before any write. The run parks at awaiting_input holding a structured PendingApproval
autoProceeds without a prompt

verify ​

An optional shell command run after a work delegation commits, e.g. npm run build && npm test. Pass/fail is reported mechanically in the change note — so "done" stops being the agent's own claim. Absent means no verification step.

Note that verify is read case-sensitively: a command's paths and flags are case-sensitive, unlike the enum keys above.

Defaults and fallback ​

ts
export const DEFAULT_POLICY: ProjectPolicy = { branch: 'new', approval: 'confirm' };

There is no global default that silently applies. An unset, missing, or invalid value falls back to the built-in safe default (new branch + confirm), unless the operator has configured a different fallback in Settings → System (defaultBranchMode, defaultApproval).

Parsing rules ​

Parsing is deliberately lenient, so a memory file that is primarily prose does not break:

  • Only the known keys are read; any other frontmatter (a tags: line, say) is ignored.
  • Inline # comments are stripped.
  • Surrounding quotes are stripped.
  • Enum values are lowercased before matching; verify preserves case.
  • An invalid enum value is not an error — it falls back to the safe default.

Validation happens at the boundary (readProjectPolicy), so every caller downstream receives a well-formed policy.

Example ​

markdown
---
branch: new
approval: confirm
verify: npm run typecheck && npm test
---

# my-app

- **Path:** `/Users/me/code/my-app`
- **GitHub:** me/my-app
- **Stack:** TypeScript, Express

## Purpose
The public API service.

## Layout & scripts
- `dev` — `tsx watch src/server.ts`
- `test` — `node --test`

## Notes / gotchas
- Requires `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`.
- Port 4000 is used by the worker; do not reuse it.

The frontmatter is the policy; everything below it is the project memory injected into the agent's prompt.

See also: Modes & Permissions · Memory & Conventions
